title: SplitStack Refurbishment - Prompt Log
subtitle: Every prompt used to analyse, plan and rebuild SplitStack for the Web Technology course
author: Mahaprabhu K

stages.Planning: Analysis of the existing project, audit report review, gap analysis and refurbishment plan
stages.Phase 0: Repository setup, hygiene and documentation tooling
stages.Review 1: HTML + CSS - static, semantic pages and a token-based design system
stages.Review 2: JavaScript - vanilla ES modules, interactivity, client-side algorithms
stages.Review 3: Node.js + MongoDB - Express REST API, Mongoose models, authentication, OCR

entries.title: Initial request from the student
entries.prompt: i have a project in my web technology course and we have made a website. i want to check everything and refurbish if needed. the project shd have these things. html + css, javascript, node js , mangodbs. for review 1-html+css, for review 2 javascript. for review 3 the rest two. i have attached a report of the existing project. i want you to analyse the repositry and then the audit report. and give a good plan for the refurshing if needed. during refurbishing i want you to document the prompts you'll use to build the project save it as a log document(word)
entries.purpose: Defines the goal: verify the project meets the course stack (HTML+CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, MongoDB) across three reviews, refurbish it, and log all prompts in a Word document.

entries.title: Analyse the repository
entries.prompt: Inventory the SplitStack repository: list every tracked file, read the git history, the dependency manifests (requirements.txt / package.json), the base HTML layout, the CSS design tokens and all JavaScript (main.js plus inline <script> blocks in templates). Identify the actual technology stack and compare it with the course requirement of HTML+CSS, JavaScript, Node.js and MongoDB.
entries.purpose: Establish ground truth about what the code really is, independent of the audit report.
entries.result: Stack is Python 3 + Flask 3.1 + SQLite with Jinja2 templates; no Node.js, no MongoDB, no package.json. Frontend JS is ~140 lines of jQuery. 25 Jinja templates cannot render without Flask. 4 user-uploaded receipt images are committed to git.
entries.verification: File listing, git log, grep for <script> tags, manual reading of base.html and main.js.

entries.title: Analyse the audit report
entries.prompt: Extract the text of SplitStack_Comprehensive_Technical_Audit.pdf (61 pages) and summarise its findings: technology stack, architecture, route inventory, database schema, security findings (SEC-01..SEC-07), test results, technical debt and the five-phase refurbishment roadmap (Phases A-E). Note anything the audit does not cover relative to the course requirements.
entries.purpose: Reuse the audit's verified findings and identify its blind spots.
entries.result: Audit confirms 48 routes, 7 blueprints, 15 SQLite tables, 47/47 tests passing. Key findings kept: incomplete light theme, --text-dim contrast 3.8:1 (fails WCAG AA), tables scroll on mobile, search/notification bell not wired, no rate limiting, no security headers, ephemeral upload storage. Blind spot: the audit never mentions that Node.js and MongoDB are required, so its Flask-specific roadmap (SQLite WAL, Flask-Limiter, PostgreSQL) does not satisfy Review 3.
entries.verification: Text extracted with pypdf; sections 2, 12-17 and Volume VI read.

entries.title: Gap analysis and refurbishment plan
entries.prompt: Produce a refurbishment plan that maps the work onto the three course reviews: Review 1 must be demonstrable with only HTML+CSS, Review 2 must add substantial vanilla JavaScript on top of the same pages, and Review 3 must replace the backend with Node.js (Express) and MongoDB while keeping every existing feature. Fold in the still-relevant audit findings. Ask the student only about decisions that are genuinely theirs: backend strategy, where MongoDB runs, feature scope, and whether to keep jQuery.
entries.purpose: Turn the analysis into an ordered plan with clear review checkpoints.
entries.result: Plan: Phase 0 setup -> Review 1 static pages + design system -> Review 2 vanilla JS with a localStorage data layer -> Review 3 Express + Mongoose REST API, with the frontend data layer switched to fetch(). Student's answers: 'do the most optimal method' for the backend (=> replace Flask with Node+MongoDB, keep Flask on a legacy branch), MongoDB Atlas free tier, keep every feature including OCR (via tesseract.js), vanilla JS modules instead of jQuery. Student also asked: 'just make sure you log everything'.
entries.verification: Decisions confirmed through a multiple-choice question in chat.

entries.title: Branching and repository hygiene
entries.prompt: Preserve the current Flask application on a local 'legacy' branch and create a 'refurbish' working branch. Stop tracking the four user-uploaded receipt images (hash-named files in uploads/receipts/) while keeping the test_invoice_* samples, deduplicate .gitignore, and add Node-specific ignores (node_modules, coverage, .env). Create the client/ folder structure (pages, css, js, assets).
entries.purpose: Protect the original work, remove private data from version control, and prepare the new layout.
entries.result: Branches legacy and refurbish created; 4 receipts untracked (still on disk); .gitignore rewritten.
entries.verification: git status shows the 4 receipts as deleted from the index and no longer as untracked files.

entries.title: Prompt-log tooling (this document)
entries.prompt: Create a Word prompt log that is easy to keep up to date: store every prompt as an entry in docs/prompt_log.json (id, date, stage, title, type, prompt, purpose, files, result, verification) and write a Node script docs/tools/build-prompt-log.js using the 'docx' npm package that renders a title page, a stage overview, a summary table of all entries, and one detailed section per entry with the prompt shown verbatim. Add an 'npm run log' script.
entries.purpose: Satisfy the requirement to document every prompt as a Word document, regenerated after each step.
entries.result: Log generator working; document regenerated after every subsequent step.
entries.verification: npm run log produces the .docx; contents read back with python-docx.
